one_line: Drukpa Kagyu master and royal advisor who helped make Hemis the great monastery of Ladakh.

appearance.age_look: Looks late 40s to early 50s, lean but sturdy, with the wiry build of a mountain traveler and long-distance walker.
appearance.face: Oval face with high cheekbones, weathered medium-brown Himalayan complexion, straight nose, a neatly trimmed short beard and moustache with a few grey strands, gentle but intense almond-shaped eyes, and a calm, slightly smiling default expression conveying composed spiritual authority.
appearance.hair: Black hair with a few grey streaks, cut short at the back and sides but slightly longer and brushed back on top; he wears a simple maroon Drukpa monk’s cap (zhwa dmar style without the grand high crown, low and soft, hugging the head) edged with a thin dark-gold border.
appearance.costume: He wears a maroon Tibetan-style monk’s chuba robe made of thick wool, ankle-length and fully wrapping the body, with a wide saffron-yellow sleeveless outer shawl (zen) draped over the left shoulder and under the right arm, plus a darker maroon under-robe visible at the collar; under the robe are dark-brown woolen trousers tucked into sturdy dark-brown leather boots suitable for Himalayan terrain, their tops lined with pale felt; over his shoulders, for travel and court visits, is a muted-ochre woolen cloak with a subtle woven diamond pattern along the edge, fastened by a small, plain bronze clasp; around his neck he wears a long dark-brown wooden mala with a few slightly larger spacer beads that rests over the saffron shawl, and on his left wrist a simple red wool thread bracelet, keeping his overall look modest yet clearly monastic and region-accurate to 16th–17th century Ladakh and central Tibet.
appearance.signature: A long, slightly weathered wooden staff topped with a small metal finial in the shape of a simple Drukpa-style vajra (double thunderbolt), the shaft wrapped in a few turns of red cloth near the grip and a short strip of faded yellow cloth tied just below the finial, carried in his right hand as both walking staff and symbol of his Drukpa authority.

ref_desc: Stag-tshang-ras-pa is a lean, weathered, bearded Himalayan monk with short black hair, a low maroon cap, deep maroon robes, a saffron shawl, brown boots, ochre cloak, wood mala, and a red-wrapped staff topped by a small vajra finial.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Stag-tshang-ras-pa (Taktsang Repa): a lean, sturdy Himalayan Drukpa monk in his late 40s–50s with an oval, weathered medium-brown face, high cheekbones, gentle intense almond eyes, a short neatly trimmed beard with a few grey strands, and short black hair brushed back with slight grey at the temples under a simple low maroon monk’s cap edged in dark gold. Show him in a thick wool deep-maroon ankle-length Tibetan chuba fully wrapping his body, a darker maroon under-robe visible at the collar, and a wide saffron-yellow zen shawl draped over his left shoulder and under his right arm. Add dark-brown woolen trousers under the robe and sturdy dark-brown leather boots lined with pale felt, plus a muted-ochre wool cloak with a subtle woven diamond border fastened at the chest with a small bronze clasp, suggesting travel in the Ladakhi Himalayas. Around his neck place a long dark-brown wooden mala with a few larger spacer beads resting over the saffron shawl, and a simple red wool thread bracelet on his left wrist. In his right hand, give him a long wooden staff wrapped with red cloth near the grip and topped with a small metal vajra finial with a short strip of faded yellow cloth tied beneath it. Use a palette dominated by deep maroon, saffron yellow, dark brown, muted ochre, and dark gold, and keep the overall look modest, dignified, historically plausible, and consistent from head to toe.
